chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The menstruating woman enters into ihram while she does not pray.' He said, 'Yes, when the time arrives, she should enter into ihram.'

key_terms.الْوَقْتَ: The time (referring to the time of entering ihram at the miqat)
key_terms.تُحْرِمُ: She enters into the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman need to pray before entering ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that menstruation does not delay the entry into the state of *ihram*, which is tied to the geographical *miqat* rather than ritual purity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between *ihram* (a state of consecration) and *salat* (prayer), affirming that a woman must assume *ihram* upon reaching the designated time even while exempt from prayer. This highlights the principle that the validity of Hajj rites is not contingent upon the continuous performance of daily prayers during the state of consecration.
